sentences.text: This revision has been filed aggrieved of the framing of charge dated 05.01.2022 by learned 1st Additional Sessions Judge Special Court Lokayukt in ST No.26/2001.

entities.text: 1st Additional Sessions Judge Special Court Lokayukt
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: At the outset, learned counsel for applicant submits that there is delay of 1256 days.

It is seen and as submitted by learned counsel for applicant that on the same date, charges were framed against the co-accused -Virendra Pandey and Vandana Pandey but both of them have been discharged by order of this Court.

Vandana Pandey was discharged in Cr.R. No.1178/2023 order dated 10.05.2023 and that order was confirmed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in SLP (Cri.)
No(s).8736/2023 dated 20.01.2025.

It is further submitted that husband of Vandana Pandey i.e. Virendra Pandey was discharged in Cr.R. No.2352/2022 dated 03.03.2023 and this order was also challenged by Lokayukt before Hon'ble Supreme Court in SLP as mentioned above.
Learned counsel for appellant submits that since two accused persons have been acquitted,
therefore, it shows the hollowness of the prosecution case.

The prosecution case was true and investigation was perfect, there was no ground by this Court and as confirmed by Hon'ble Supreme Court to 2 CRR-5503-2025 confirm their discharge, therefore, in the facts and circumstances and for the reasons that they were innocent and there is no incriminating oral or documentary evidence

,
the applicant should be also discharged.

Learned counsel for applicant very fairly submits that all the cases related to the year 2009 to 2013 in Mahakaushal Paramedical College in which Virendra Pandey and Vandana Pandey were President and Vice President of the Society of the College and allegations against them were that by forgery, they got admission of certain students in D.M.L.T. Course and obtained money for scholarship from the Tribal Development Department.
Charges against the applicant was framed under Sections 120-B, 420/34, 409/34, 467/34, 468/34, 471/34 of IPC.

sentences.text: It is submitted that while Virendra Pandey and Vandana Pandey were President and Vice President of a Society in the college whereas the present applicant - G.P. Gautam was the Principal.
It is a private institution.
Therefore, it is seen prima facie to this Court that Principal is head of the institution for running various administrative as well as academic and financial activities.
President and other persons are not involved in day to day work i.e. job of the Principal.
So there is a fundamental difference in the legal characteristics of applicant - G.P. Gautam and the co-accused, who have been discharged.

The Law regarding discharge is well settled by Hon'ble Supreme Court recently in the judgment dated 18 May 2023 in Cr.A No. 1399/2023 -Captain Manjeet Singh Virdhi (Retired) v. Hussain Mohammed Shattaf and others [2023 LiveLaw (SC) 462] wherein Hon'ble Supreme Court has held in 3 CRR-5503-2025 paragraphs 11 and paragraph 12 thus:
11.

entities.text: Cr.A No. 1399/2023 -Captain Manjeet Singh Virdhi (Retired) v. Hussain Mohammed Shattaf and others [2023 LiveLaw (SC) 462]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The law on issue as to what is to be considered at the time of discharge of an accused is well settled.
It is a case in which the Trial Court had not yet framed the charges.
Immediately after filing of chargesheet, application for discharge was filed.
The settled proposition of law is that at the stage of hearing on the charges entire evidence produced by the prosecution is to be believed.
In case no offence is made out then only an accused can be discharged.
Truthfulness, sufficiency and acceptability of the material produced can be done only at the stage of trial.
At the stage of charge, the Court has to satisfy that a prima facie case is made out against the accused persons.

Interference of the Court at that stage is required only if there is strong reasons to hold that in case the trial is allowed to proceed, the same would amount to abuse of process of the Court.
12.

The law on the point has been summarised in a recent judgment of this Court in State of Rajasthan v.
Ashok Kumar Kashyap2.

entities.text:
State of Rajasthan v.
Ashok Kumar Kashyap2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Relevant paras are extracted below: -

In P. Vijayan v. State of Kerala, (2010) 2 SCC 398, this Court had an occasion to consider Section 227 CrPC What is required to be considered at the time of framing of the charge and/or considering the discharge application has been considered elaborately in the said decision.

entities.text: P. Vijayan v. State of Kerala, (2010) 2 SCC 398
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is observed and held that at the stage of Section 227, the Judge has merely to sift the evidence in order to find out whether or not there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.

It is observed that in other words, the sufficiency of grounds would take within its fold the nature of the evidence recorded by the police or the documents produced before the court which ex facie disclose that there are suspicious circumstances against the accused so as to frame a charge against him.
It is further observed that if the Judge comes to a conclusion that there is sufficient ground to proceed, he will frame a charge under Section 228 CrPC, if not, he will discharge the accused.

11.2. In the recent decision of this Court in State of Karnataka v. M.R. Hiremath,
(2019) 7 SCC 515, one of us (D.Y. Chandrachud, J.) speaking for the Bench has observed and held in para 25 as under:
4 CRR-5503-2025 "25.

sentences.text: The High Court [M.R. Hiremath v. State, 2017 SCC OnLine Kar 4970] ought to have been cognizant of the fact that the trial court was dealing with an application for discharge under the provisions of Section 239 CrPC.

entities.text: M.R. Hiremath v. State, 2017 SCC OnLine Kar 4970]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The parameters which govern the exercise of this jurisdiction have found expression in several decisions of this Court.

It is a settled principle of law that at the stage of considering an application for discharge the court must proceed on the assumption that the material which has been brought on the record by the prosecution is true and evaluate the material in order to determine whether the facts emerging from the material, taken on its face value, disclose the existence of the ingredients necessary to constitute the offence.

In State of T.N. v. N. Suresh Rajan, (2014) 11 SCC 709, adverting to the earlier decisions on the subject, this Court held:
'29. ...

entities.text: State of T.N. v. N. Suresh Rajan, (2014) 11 SCC 709
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At this stage, probative value of the materials has to be gone into and the court is not expected to go deep into the matter and hold that the materials would not warrant a conviction.
In our opinion, what needs to be considered is whether there is a ground for presuming that the offence has been committed and not whether a ground for convicting the accused has been made out.

To put it differently, if the court thinks that the accused might have committed the offence on the basis of the materials on record on its probative value, it can frame the charge; though for conviction, the court has to come to the conclusion that the accused has committed the offence.
The law does not permit a mini trial at this stage."

What was the role of the previously discharged accused and what is the role of the present applicant that can be ascertained only during trial, otherwise a situation may come wherein a serious financial crime may have been committed in any institution and all are discharged.
It is not the case of the applicant that he was not involved and certain other persons naming X, Y & Z were involved.
If that was the case, the situation may have been different but that is not the case.
No other person has been named as a culprit.

At this stage, another argument is made by learned counsel for 5 CRR-5503-2025 applicant that there was no unlawful gain even one paisa made to the applicant and no loss of even one paisa is caused to the government and on the next date of hearing,
this fact can be verified from the counsel for the Lokayukt that whether any loss was caused to government or not.
